lesson.title: Functions
lesson.driving_question: How can a named block of code be written once and used again?
lesson.primary_concept_family: A function stores a reusable procedure and a function call runs it.
lesson.concept_budget: Define and call one parameter-free function; parameters and returned values are deferred to Lesson 13.
misconceptions: def creates a function but does not run its body immediately.
The indented lines belong to the function body.
The function must be defined before the call runs.
lesson.progression_note: The learner moves repeated output into a named block, then calls the block again. Lesson 13 will add inputs and results to the function.

shared_program.code:
def show_greeting():
    print("Hello, Python learner!")
show_greeting()
print("Welcome to Python.")
shared_program.expected_output:
Hello, Python learner!
Welcome to Python.

primm.prompt: Recall: What does indentation show? How can a loop save repeated code? What does a name help us remember?
Predict which lines display when the function is defined, when it is called, and when the final print() runs. Explain when the function body runs.
Run the supplied file. Compare the order of the two messages with your prediction and explain one match or mismatch.

questions: Why does Python not run a function body when it first reads the def statement?
What happens if the function name is written without parentheses where a call is intended?
Why must the function body be indented?
Which two messages appear, and in what order?

primm.prompt: Change the example by adding a second function called show_rules() that displays "Save your work often." and "Ask for help when stuck." Call show_rules() after show_greeting() and before the final message.

A greeting is useful more than once. Call show_greeting() a second time so "Hello, Python learner!" appears twice. Keep the final "Welcome to Python." message. Predict the number of greetings before you run the program.
Build one no-input function called show_tip() that displays a Python tip of your choice. Call it twice; the same tip should appear two times.
Repair the undefined message used inside the function, then run the corrected greeting program.

blocks.definition: A named block of code which performs a task. The indented body is stored until the function is called.
The keyword which starts a function definition. The line ends with a colon.
The indented lines under the def line. These lines belong to the function.
The function name followed by parentheses. A call runs the stored function body.
Define the greeting once, call it when the program needs the greeting, and keep the rest of the program readable.
blocks.example:
def show_greeting():
    print("Hello, Python learner!")
show_greeting()
print("Welcome to Python.")
